hero.headline: Secretary of State Rubio questioned on Iran war and gas prices in budget hearings
hero.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio faced questioning from House Democrats during congressional budget hearings about the Trump administration's stance on Israel's nuclear weapons program. Thirty Democratic lawmakers sent a letter to Rubio arguing that the United States must publicly acknowledge that Israel possesses nuclear weapons, particularly as Washington collaborates with Israel on military operations against Iran.

The Democrats, led by Texas Representative Joaquin Castro, contend that the continued ambiguity surrounding Israel's nuclear capabilities is unsustainable given current circumstances. "We are, in the fullest sense, fighting this war side by side with a country whose potential nuclear weapons program the United States government officially refuses to acknowledge," the letter states.

The lawmakers emphasized that Congress needs complete information about the nuclear balance in the Middle East and potential risks of escalation. They noted that the Trump administration has not provided adequate details about planning and contingencies related to nuclear scenarios in the region.

Israel has never publicly confirmed its nuclear weapons program, and no U.S. administration has officially acknowledged it, despite substantial evidence of its existence. The program dates back to the 1950s and received assistance from countries including France and apartheid-era South Africa. American presidents have historically avoided discussing the subject directly.

However, several government officials have essentially confirmed Israel's nuclear capabilities. In a 2006 confirmation hearing, then-nominee Robert Gates said Iran was "surrounded by powers with nuclear weapons: Pakistan to their east, the Russians to the north, the Israelis to the west and us in the Persian Gulf." Similarly, former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert told a German broadcaster that Iran was "aspiring to have nuclear weapons, as America, France, Israel, Russia."

The Democrats pointed out that Israeli officials have occasionally alluded to the weapons. In 2023, Israeli Heritage Minister Amichai Eliyahu suggested using a nuclear bomb in Gaza was "one of the possibilities" following attacks on October 7.

The Democrats noted that Trump administration officials have refused to discuss the issue publicly. When Representative Castro asked Under Secretary of State Thomas DiNanno about Israel's nuclear capabilities at a March congressional hearing, DiNanno declined to answer.

The lawmakers called for consistent treatment of all nations regarding nuclear weapons transparency. "The United States openly acknowledges the nuclear weapons programs of the United Kingdom, France, India, Pakistan, Russia, China, and North Korea. We ask that Israel be held to the same standard as any other foreign country," the letter reads.

The Democrats also warned that continued ambiguity complicates nuclear nonproliferation efforts in the Middle East. Saudi Arabia's crown prince has stated his country would pursue nuclear weapons if Iran develops them, making transparent discussion of Israel's capabilities increasingly important for regional security discussions.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Proposes 10 Percent Tariffs on Multiple Trading Partners
cards.teaser: The US government announced plans for new levies of at least 10 percent on dozens of countries over forced labor concerns.
cards.body:
The Trump administration announced tariffs of 10 percent or higher targeting approximately 60 trading partners, including Canada, Mexico, and the European Union. The administration cited forced labor practices in supply chains as justification for the levies, representing an expansion of US trade barriers.

The proposal marks a return to aggressive tariff policies characteristic of the earlier Trump administration. India indicated it remains engaged with the US as it reviews the proposed measures.

cards.headline: Bill Pulte moves from mortgage chief to acting national intelligence director
cards.teaser: The Senate Intelligence Committee's top Democrat discussed Pulte's transition to the intelligence role.
cards.body:
Bill Pulte, who led the Federal Housing Finance Agency, has been named acting Director of National Intelligence by President Trump. In this role, he will oversee the intelligence community, including the CIA, NSA, and FBI.

Senator Mark Warner of Virginia, the ranking Democrat on the Senate Intelligence Committee, discussed Pulte's appointment in an interview. Pulte's previous work focused on housing and mortgage policy before his move to the intelligence position.

cards.headline: Trump administration scraps $1.8 billion payout fund after Republican opposition
cards.teaser: The Justice Department will not proceed with a fund intended to compensate individuals who claimed government wrongdoing.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has abandoned a $1.8 billion compensation fund designed to provide payouts to individuals who claimed the government weaponized federal agencies against them. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the decision while testifying before House lawmakers.

The fund faced significant opposition from Republican lawmakers who objected to its scope and structure. Following the pushback from members of the president's own party, the Justice Department decided not to proceed with the program.

cards.headline: SpaceX plans $75 billion IPO at $135 per share
cards.body:
SpaceX is planning to go public with a $1.75 trillion valuation, according to details revealed in a flotation prospectus. The company will seek $75 billion in the offering, with shares priced at $135 each. The IPO is targeted for next month and will be structured as an all-primary offering, meaning all shares sold will be newly issued rather than from existing shareholders.

The company encompasses multiple business units beyond its core rocket launch operations. SpaceX's divisions include its space segment, which handles rocket launches for NASA and other clients; Starlink, its satellite broadband service; xAI, Musk's artificial intelligence startup; and the social media platform X, formerly Twitter.

Despite its massive valuation, SpaceX is currently unprofitable. The company lost $4.9 billion in 2025 while generating $18.7 billion in revenue. Losses widened in early 2026, with the company posting a $4.3 billion loss in the first quarter compared to a $528 million loss in the same period last year. The AI unit was the primary driver of losses, losing $6.4 billion last year due to expenses like building and operating datacentres for the Grok AI tool. Starlink was the only profitable segment in the first three months of 2026.

Capital expenditure totaled $20.7 billion, with the xAI unit accounting for $12.7 billion of that total. SpaceX has constructed a large datacentre called Colossus to support its AI operations.

The prospectus includes ambitious long-term goals that go beyond typical corporate plans. SpaceX lists potential future markets including space tourism, energy production and manufacturing on the moon and Mars, and asteroid mining. The company acknowledges these markets do not currently exist but expects them to develop over time. More near-term, SpaceX plans to launch space-based datacentres powered by solar energy as early as 2028, an initiative the prospectus calls "orbital compute."

Elon Musk will maintain extraordinary control over SpaceX following the IPO. He will hold approximately 85 percent of voting power through ownership of class B shares, which carry 10 votes each compared to one vote per class A share held by other investors. This structure makes it extremely difficult to remove Musk from leadership.

Musk stands to accumulate additional wealth from the offering. He has been granted one billion class B shares that vest if SpaceX establishes a permanent human colony on Mars with at least one million inhabitants and achieves a market capitalization of $7.5 trillion. He received another grant of 302 million class B shares in March that vest upon completion of space-based datacentres delivering 100 terawatts of computing power annually.

cards.headline: Drone Strike Kills Seven on Bus in Russian-Controlled Ukraine
cards.teaser: A bus traveling between Moscow and Crimea was hit by a drone in Russian-occupied territory.
cards.body:
Seven people were killed when a drone struck a bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in Russian-occupied Crimea, according to local officials. The attack targeted civilian transportation on the long-distance route connecting the Russian capital with the occupied peninsula.

Russian officials confirmed the deaths and attributed the incident to a drone strike, though they did not identify the type of aircraft or who was responsible for the attack.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden Cabinet member secured the nomination and could become the first female Native American governor.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. The former Biden administration official is now positioned to compete in the general election this fall.

If elected in November, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in U.S. history.

cards.headline: Ukraine Targets St. Petersburg During Economic Forum
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces launched strikes on St. Petersburg as Russia's annual economic summit began in the city.
cards.body:
Ukraine conducted strikes on St. Petersburg as Russia's major economic forum opened in the city. The attacks coincided with the start of an event often compared to the World Economic Forum in Davos, where Russian President Vladimir Putin hosts international business leaders and officials.

The timing of the strikes appeared designed to disrupt the high-profile gathering and demonstrate Ukraine's ability to reach major Russian cities far from the front lines. St. Petersburg, Russia's second-largest city, sits more than 600 miles from Ukrainian-controlled territory.

cards.headline: Thousands Protest Kushner Resort Project in Albania
cards.teaser: Large demonstrations erupted in Albania against a luxury resort development linked to Jared Kushner.
cards.body:
Thousands of protesters took to the streets in Albania to oppose a resort project connected to Jared Kushner, son-in-law of President Trump. The development has triggered an anti-corruption investigation and sparked violent clashes as demonstrators raised concerns about the project's environmental impact and approval process.

The resort is planned for a protected coastal area, and critics allege the Albanian government misled parliament about the project's scope and environmental implications. The controversy has created a new obstacle for Albania's efforts to join the European Union, with the development plans drawing scrutiny from EU officials.

cards.headline: Death of Handcuffed British Student Sparks Protests and Investigation
cards.teaser: British authorities are investigating police who handcuffed Henry Nowak, a student who died from a stab wound while in custody.
cards.body:
UK officials launched an investigation into police officers who handcuffed Henry Nowak, a student who was dying from a stab wound. The case has triggered widespread protests and increasingly heated political debate about police conduct and racial bias in law enforcement.

Demonstrations erupted in Southampton following Nowak's death, with some protests turning violent as crowds clashed with police. A government minister condemned the rioting while simultaneously calling for a review of police anti-racism guidance. Protesters have drawn comparisons to other high-profile cases of police conduct during medical emergencies.

The administration cited forced labor practices in supply chains as justification for the levies, representing an expansion of US trade barriers.

cards.headline: Documents Show Shell Operated Polluting Pipeline in Nigeria for Years
cards.teaser: Shell continued pumping oil through a Nigerian pipeline despite internal evidence of pollution, according to newly revealed documents.
cards.body:
Shell operated an oil pipeline in Nigeria for years despite internal evidence of environmental pollution, according to newly disclosed documents. The revelations highlight concerns about the company's environmental oversight in one of its major operational regions.

Shell acknowledged the documents but disputed their implications, arguing they lack crucial context about Nigeria's complex operating environment at the time. The company did not challenge the authenticity of the records.

cards.teaser: Germany faces a tight vote as it campaigns against Austria for a rotating seat on the UN Security Council.

hero.teaser: The Justice Department will not proceed with a fund intended to compensate individuals who claimed government wrongdoing.
hero.body:
The Trump administration has abandoned a $1.8 billion compensation fund designed to provide payouts to individuals who claimed the government weaponized federal agencies against them. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the decision while testifying before House lawmakers.

The fund faced significant opposition from Republican lawmakers who objected to its scope and structure. Following the pushback from members of the president's own party, the Justice Department decided not to proceed with the program.

cards.headline: California governor primary remains too close to call
cards.teaser: Two Democrats and one Republican are locked in tight competition to advance to the November general election.
cards.body:
California's gubernatorial primary remained undecided Tuesday night as votes continued to be counted. Early results showed Republican Steve Hilton and Democrats Xavier Becerra and Tom Steyer leading the crowded field, with the two top finishers advancing to November's general election under the state's top-two primary system.

The close contest prompted two Democratic candidates to concede: San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan and former Los Angeles Mayor Antonio Villaraigosa both withdrew from the race shortly after polls closed.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advances to November runoff
cards.teaser: Bass will face a challenger in the general election after winning the most votes but not a majority in the primary.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass won the primary election but fell short of the 50 percent threshold needed to avoid a runoff. She will advance to November's general election to defend her seat.

Bass will face one of two challengers: Republican Spencer Pratt, a former reality TV star, or Democrat Nithya Raman, a city council member. The race between Pratt and Raman to determine Bass's opponent was still undecided as of Tuesday evening.

cards.headline: Seven killed in drone strike on bus in Russian-controlled Ukraine
cards.teaser: The bus was traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in Russian-occupied Crimea when it was hit.
cards.body:
A drone struck a bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in Russian-occupied Crimea, killing seven people, according to a Russian official. The bus was on a route connecting the Russian capital with the Crimean peninsula, which Russia has controlled since 2014.

The official confirmed the death toll but did not identify the victims or specify who launched the drone.

cards.headline: Primary elections set midterm matchups in six states
cards.teaser: Voters in California, Iowa, New Jersey, and three other states cast ballots to determine general election candidates.
cards.body:
Voters in six states participated in primary elections to determine nominees for November's midterm races. California held a competitive gubernatorial primary where Republicans and Democrats competed together, with two Democrats and one Republican in close contention for the top two spots that will advance to the general election.

In Iowa, Democrat Josh Turek won the nomination to face Trump-backed Republican Ashley Hinson in a bid to flip the Senate seat. The Iowa results drew Democratic attention as the party seeks to gain ground in a state that has shifted Republican in recent years.

cards.headline: Shell operated Nigeria pipeline despite pollution evidence, documents show
cards.teaser: Internal documents reveal the oil company continued pumping oil through a pipeline for years after learning of environmental damage.
cards.body:
Newly disclosed documents reveal that Shell continued pumping oil through a Nigerian pipeline for years despite internal evidence of pollution. The records indicate the company was aware of environmental damage caused by the pipeline operations during this period.

Shell acknowledged the documents but disputed their implications, stating they lack critical context about the complex operating environment in Nigeria at the time. The company did not challenge the authenticity of the materials.

cards.headline: Royal Navy helicopter crashes into field, road closed
cards.teaser: The A386 between the A30 and Okehampton remains shut following the incident.
cards.body:
A Royal Navy helicopter crashed into a field, prompting authorities to close a major road in the area. The A386 between the A30 and Okehampton was shut down as a result of the incident.

Authorities have not released information about casualties or the cause of the crash. The closure affects a stretch of road used to connect the A30 trunk road with the town of Okehampton in Devon.

cards.headline: Seven states sue Trump administration over offshore wind farm deal
cards.teaser: Seven states filed suit challenging a nearly $1 billion payment to halt an offshore wind project.
cards.body:
Seven states, including New York, have filed a lawsuit challenging a Trump administration deal that paid TotalEnergies nearly $1 billion to cancel offshore wind farm projects along the Atlantic coast. The states argue the administration lacked proper authority to make the payment.

The legal action represents a clash between state governments backing renewable energy development and federal policy aimed at halting offshore wind expansion. The states contend the agreement was improper and designed to undermine wind energy projects that had already been approved and were in development.

cards.headline: CBS News fires Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: CBS removed the veteran journalist after months of staff tensions with the network's editor in chief.
cards.body:
CBS News fired Scott Pelley, a veteran correspondent for 60 Minutes and former anchor of CBS Evening News, as part of a broader overhaul of the show. The network also dismissed the program's executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

During a staff meeting, Pelley directly criticized Bari Weiss, CBS News's editor-in-chief, over the dismissals. The firings reflect ongoing tensions between newsroom staff and editorial leadership at the network.

cards.headline: Stock futures hold steady after S&P 500 hits another record
cards.teaser: Stock futures showed little movement after the S&P 500 closed at a new all-time high.
cards.body:
Stock futures remained relatively unchanged after the S&P 500 index closed at another record high. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 both ended at fresh records, extending their longest winning streaks of the year. The continued rally has been driven primarily by artificial intelligence stocks, which have sustained the market's upward momentum.

Wall Street's gains have been concentrated in technology companies working on AI development and infrastructure. The S&P 500's performance continues to rely heavily on a narrow group of stocks rather than broad market participation. Analysts note that while American stock markets are surging, the rally remains focused on the AI sector rather than reflecting widespread economic gains across industries.

cards.headline: Nvidia CEO calls Marvell the next trillion-dollar company
cards.teaser: Shares of Marvell and other chipmakers hit 52-week highs after Jensen Huang predicted major growth for the company.
cards.body:
Marvell Technology's stock surged to a 52-week high after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang predicted the chipmaker would become the next trillion-dollar company. Broadcom and Hewlett Packard Enterprise also reached 52-week highs in the same trading session. Huang described Marvell as an essential company positioned for significant valuation growth.

The stock movement reflects continued investor enthusiasm for companies involved in AI chip design and infrastructure. Some market analysts expressed caution about the rapid rise, with at least one noting concern about stocks climbing based on predictions rather than current fundamentals. The gains added Marvell to the list of AI-related stocks driving broader market performance.

cards.headline: Oil prices rise as US and Iran trade strikes
cards.teaser: Oil prices climbed as hostilities between the United States and Iran intensified, though stocks showed mixed results.
cards.body:
Oil prices jumped following fresh military exchanges between the United States and Iran. US forces fired a Hellfire missile at a tanker attempting to breach the American blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, then repelled Iranian attacks in the region and struck sites on Iran's Qeshm Island. Iran responded with drone strikes that damaged Kuwait's international airport, forcing a suspension of traffic.

The escalating hostilities have disrupted diplomatic efforts, with ceasefire negotiations between Washington and Tehran now in jeopardy. Stock markets showed mixed responses to the tensions, while the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development warned that the Middle East conflict's economic consequences will persist for some time.

cards.headline: Japan's Nikkei reaches record high as tech stocks rally
cards.teaser: Tokyo's Nikkei 225 index topped 68,000 for the first time, driven by gains in technology shares.

hero.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft launch RTX Spark laptops with AI chips
hero.body:
Nvidia has unveiled the RTX Spark, a new "superchip" designed to bring artificial intelligence capabilities directly into laptops and desktop computers. The move marks a significant expansion for the dominant AI chip maker, which has built its reputation on data center processors, into the consumer PC market.

The RTX Spark combines a microprocessor with a graphics chip, developed in collaboration with Taiwan's MediaTek. Unlike current AI applications that rely on cloud computing, the RTX Spark enables AI agents to run locally on individual machines. This approach reduces dependence on internet connectivity while potentially improving performance and privacy for users.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced the chip at the Computex conference in Taiwan, describing it as a fundamental reimagining of the PC "for the first time in 40 years." He highlighted an ambitious vision in which AI agents could navigate computers autonomously, potentially replacing traditional mouse and keyboard interactions. The company emphasized that despite its power, computers using the RTX Spark will remain thin and light.

The partnership with Microsoft builds on their three-year collaboration. Computer manufacturers including Dell, Lenovo, Asus and HP will integrate the RTX Spark chip into their devices running Windows. Microsoft demonstrated the technology at its Build conference and announced plans for a desktop version of the RTX Spark platform aimed at software developers, along with new Linux development tools for Windows.

This launch intensifies competition in the AI chip sector. Nvidia's entry into consumer PCs puts the company directly against Intel, Apple, Qualcomm and AMD, all of which produce processors for personal computers. Intel announced plans to ship its own AI chip later this year, featuring cheaper memory and cooling technology.

Analysts view the RTX Spark as potentially transformative for the PC industry. Neil Shah, co-founder of Counterpoint Research, compared the announcement to watershed technological moments including the iPhone and ChatGPT, suggesting that AI personal computers running agents will eventually become commonplace in households.

The timing reflects broader industry momentum toward edge AI, where processing happens on devices rather than in distant data centers. This shift could reshape how people interact with computers, moving from traditional app-based computing toward AI-assisted productivity.

While the RTX Spark represents a strategic opportunity for Nvidia, industry observers note that building a meaningful consumer PC business will require time. For now, Nvidia's financial performance remains heavily dependent on data center demand, where the company maintains overwhelming market dominance. The launch of the RTX Spark nevertheless signals the company's determination to compete across multiple layers of the AI technology stack, extending its influence beyond the infrastructure that powers AI development and into the devices consumers use daily.

cards.headline: Sony announces God of War game following Kratos' wife Faye
cards.teaser: Santa Monica Studio revealed God of War Laufey, a spinoff centered on Kratos' late wife Faye.
cards.body:
Sony announced God of War Laufey during its State of Play presentation. The new title will be developed by Santa Monica Studio and is coming to PlayStation 5, though an official release date has not yet been set.

The game marks a new direction for the franchise by shifting focus to Laufey, known as Faye, the wife of series protagonist Kratos. The announcement included gameplay footage that offered viewers their first look at the upcoming title.

cards.headline: Insomniac shows new Wolverine game footage with X-Men characters
cards.teaser: Developers detailed combat mechanics, gore settings, and character appearances for the upcoming Wolverine game.
cards.body:
Insomniac Games unveiled new footage from its upcoming Wolverine game, showcasing the claw combat mechanics and gameplay systems. The presentation included details about X-Men character appearances and confirmed that players can experience Logan's death despite his regenerative abilities.

The developers revealed a low-gore option for the game, allowing players to reduce graphic violence while maintaining the character's intense fighting style. The title is in development for PlayStation 5, extending Insomniac's collaboration with Sony following the success of its Spider-Man franchise.

cards.headline: Ubisoft remaking Rayman Legends in 3D, launches in October
cards.teaser: Rayman Legends Retold brings the 2013 platformer into three dimensions with a planned October 1 release.
cards.body:
Ubisoft announced Rayman Legends Retold, a 3D remake of the 2013 platformer Rayman Legends. The game is scheduled to launch on October 1 across multiple platforms. Ubisoft explained its decision to revisit the title, which was originally released as a 2D side-scrolling game and received positive reviews.

The remake will target 60 frames per second performance on Nintendo Switch 2 and maintain content parity with versions on other platforms. Ubisoft stated that all content from the original game will be included in the remake. The company provided hands-on demonstrations showing how the classic gameplay translates to three-dimensional environments.

cards.headline: Venus and Jupiter visible together in evening sky this week
cards.teaser: The two planets appear close together in the night sky during early June.
cards.body:
Venus and Jupiter are visible in close proximity in the evening sky throughout early June, creating a double-planet viewing opportunity. The two planets appear to meet from Earth's perspective, though they remain millions of miles apart in space. Multiple astronomy guides have highlighted the event as a notable sky-watching opportunity for the month.

The encounter is visible without special equipment in the evening hours. Observers in North America can see both planets in the western sky after sunset. The alignment represents a regular astronomical occurrence when planetary orbits create the appearance of closeness from Earth's vantage point.

cards.headline: Stuntman series returns with Hollywood movie tie-ins for PS5
cards.teaser: The driving game franchise reappears with licensed vehicles and stunts from Universal films.
cards.body:
A new Stuntman game titled Stuntman Hollywood was announced for PlayStation 5, reviving the driving series focused on performing movie stunts. The game will feature licensed content from Universal films including the Fast and Furious franchise and Back to the Future. Sony revealed the title during its State of Play presentation.

The game centers on performing stunt driving sequences inspired by Hollywood action films. Players will use vehicles from the licensed movie properties to complete driving challenges. The Stuntman series previously appeared on PlayStation 2 and PlayStation 3 before going dormant for over a decade.

cards.headline: Cyera approaches $12 billion valuation in new funding round
cards.teaser: The cybersecurity company is raising approximately $300 million despite reporting operating losses.
cards.body:
Cyera is nearing completion of a $300 million funding round that would value the cybersecurity company at $12 billion. Evolution Equity Partners is leading the investment. The valuation represents a multiple of 80 times annual recurring revenue, a high ratio that reflects investor confidence in the company's growth potential.

The funding comes despite Cyera reporting operating losses, a common situation for fast-growing technology companies

hero.headline: Patriots Acquire Wide Receiver A.J. Brown from Eagles in Trade
hero.body:
The New England Patriots have acquired wide receiver A.J. Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in a trade. Brown participated in his first practice with the Patriots during organized team activities, marking a significant roster change for both franchises.

The trade prompted mixed reactions at Eagles OTAs as Philadelphia moves forward without one of its top offensive weapons. Brown had been a key component of the Eagles' passing game, and his departure represents a notable shift in the team's offensive strategy. The Eagles will need to adjust their game plan as they turn the page following the transaction.

For the Patriots, the acquisition brings an established receiver to their roster. Analysis of Brown's first practice with New England offered early insights into how the team plans to integrate him into their offensive scheme. The move gives the Patriots a proven target as they look to strengthen their passing attack.

The trade creates both winners and losers across the league. Teams and players who benefit from the move gain new opportunities, while others face challenges adjusting to the reshuffled landscape. The blockbuster deal has implications for both teams' offensive depth charts and strategic approaches heading into the season.

Brown's arrival in New England addresses a key positional need for the Patriots while forcing the Eagles to redistribute targets among their remaining receivers. Both organizations will spend the coming weeks adapting to the change as they continue their offseason preparation programs.

cards.headline: Golden Knights Rally Past Hurricanes 5-4 in Stanley Cup Final Game 1
cards.teaser: Vegas scored a comeback victory over Carolina in the opening game of the Stanley Cup Final.
cards.body:
Tomas Hertl scored the go-ahead goal in the third period to lift the Vegas Golden Knights to a 5-4 victory over the Carolina Hurricanes in Game 1 of the Stanley Cup Final in Raleigh, North Carolina. The Hurricanes squandered an early two-goal lead before Vegas completed the comeback.

Shea Theodore led the Golden Knights with three points, while Brett Howden, Ivan Barbashev, and William Karlsson also scored. The win puts Vegas three victories away from capturing their second Stanley Cup championship and gives them a 1-0 series lead heading into Game 2.

cards.headline: Spurs Face Knicks in NBA Finals Matchup
cards.teaser: San Antonio and New York are set to compete for the NBA championship.
cards.body:
The San Antonio Spurs and New York Knicks will meet in the 2026 NBA Finals, beginning Wednesday. This marks the Knicks' first finals appearance since 1999, as they pursue their first championship since 1973. Victor Wembanyama leads the Spurs in the series matchup.

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has repealed bedtime restrictions for the city's children during the Knicks' finals run, demonstrating the team's significance to the community and the mayor's support for the hometown squad.

cards.headline: Red Sox Pitcher Garrett Crochet Diagnosed With Lat Strain
cards.teaser: Boston's Garrett Crochet has been shut down from throwing after an MRI revealed a low-grade lat strain.
cards.body:
Garrett Crochet has been diagnosed with a low-grade strain in his left lat muscle after undergoing an MRI. The Red Sox pitcher experienced tightness in the area and has been placed on the injured list. Crochet has been shut down from throwing activities as he addresses what the team described as a very minor setback.

The injury comes during a stretch when the Red Sox bats have been productive. Crochet spoke about the IL stint and his efforts to return to action. The timeframe for his return will depend on how the lat muscle responds to treatment and rest.

cards.headline: Ferrari Driver Charles Leclerc Signs New Long-Term Contract
cards.teaser: Charles Leclerc has agreed to a new multi-year deal with Ferrari ahead of the Monaco Grand Prix.
cards.body:
Charles Leclerc has agreed to a new long-term contract with Ferrari, the Formula 1 team announced ahead of this weekend's Monaco Grand Prix. The Monaco native will continue racing for the Italian team in the seasons ahead.

The deal represents a significant commitment from both Leclerc and Ferrari as the team pursues its championship ambitions.

cards.headline: Iowa State's Milan Momcilovic Transfers to Kentucky Basketball
cards.teaser: Former Iowa State star Milan Momcilovic has committed to play for Kentucky.
cards.body:
Milan Momcilovic has transferred from Iowa State to Kentucky, giving the Wildcats a significant addition to their roster. The move prompted national media reactions, with observers noting the commitment brings optimism to the Kentucky program. Momcilovic's decision followed what reports described as a high-stakes recruitment process.

The transfer provides Kentucky with a major boost in college basketball rankings for the 2026-27 season. Momcilovic's arrival places the Wildcats in the Top 25 And 1 rankings. Kentucky secured the commitment after competing with other programs for the forward's services.

cards.headline: Aston Villa Forward Kirsty Hanson Set to Join Tottenham
cards.teaser: Kirsty Hanson will move from Aston Villa to Tottenham after finishing as Villa's top scorer.
cards.body:
Aston Villa's top scorer Kirsty Hanson is moving to Tottenham following a strong season in the Women's Super League. The forward made an impact at Villa and has now secured a move to Spurs.

The transfer strengthens Tottenham's attacking options as they prepare for the upcoming campaign.

hero.headline: Peabo Bryson, Grammy-Winning Disney Vocalist, Dies
hero.body:
Peabo Bryson, the Grammy Award-winning singer best known for his performances of Disney movie themes, has died. The news prompted tributes from fellow artists, including Celine Dion, who described herself as heartbroken by his passing.

Bryson gained widespread recognition for his work on Disney soundtracks, including the Oscar-winning song "Beauty and the Beast," which he performed as a duet with Dion for the 1991 animated film. He also recorded "A Whole New World" for the 1992 film "Aladdin," another collaboration that became one of Disney's most recognized songs. Both performances earned him Grammy Awards and established him as a defining voice in animated film music during the 1990s.

Born in South Carolina, Bryson built a career that spanned several decades in R&B and pop music. Before his Disney work brought him mainstream fame, he had already established himself as a successful recording artist with a string of romantic ballads. His smooth vocal style made him a natural fit for the emotional themes that accompanied Disney's animated features during their renaissance period.

Dion's tribute highlighted the personal and professional bond the two singers shared through their collaborations. Their duet on "Beauty and the Beast" became a cultural touchstone and introduced Bryson's voice to a new generation of listeners. The song reached number nine on the Billboard Hot 100 and won the Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals in 1993.

Bryson's influence extended beyond his Disney work, as he recorded numerous solo albums and collaborated with other major artists throughout his career. His contributions to film music helped define the sound of Disney's animated classics during a pivotal era for the studio. The cause of death has not been disclosed.

cards.headline: Scott Pelley Fired from 60 Minutes, Criticizes CBS Leadership
cards.teaser: The veteran journalist accused the network of abandoning its principles following his dismissal.
cards.body:
CBS News fired Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes as part of a broader overhaul that also removed the show's executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega. During a staff meeting, Pelley directly criticized Bari Weiss, the network's editor-in-chief, over the decision.

In a statement, Pelley said the leadership of 60 Minutes is no longer recognizable and that the principles he values are gone. He stated his departure was necessary given what he described as a collapse of values at the news program.

cards.headline: Giorgio Locatelli to Replace John Torode on Celebrity MasterChef
cards.teaser: The Italian restaurateur will join Grace Dent as co-host of the cooking competition series.
cards.body:
Giorgio Locatelli will become the new co-host of Celebrity MasterChef, replacing John Torode who departed the show last year. The Italian restaurateur will work alongside Grace Dent on the series, which features celebrities competing in culinary challenges.

Locatelli brings decades of restaurant experience to the hosting role. His appointment represents a significant change for the program, which had featured Torode as a mainstay of the judging panel. The announcement was made as production prepares for the upcoming season of the celebrity edition of the cooking competition.

cards.headline: Indian Film Board Clears Oscar-Nominated Film After Blocking Release
cards.teaser: "The Voice of Hind Rajab" can now be released after weeks of controversy over its initial censorship.
cards.body:
India's Central Board of Film Certification reversed its decision to block the release of "The Voice of Hind Rajab," the Oscar-nominated feature film directed by Kaouther Ben Hania. The board had initially prevented the film from being shown in theaters in March, citing concerns about its politically sensitive content.

The clearance comes after weeks of controversy in India surrounding the censorship of the film. The movie tells the real story of Hind Rajab, though the board had previously deemed it too controversial for theatrical distribution. The reversal represents a significant shift in the board's position on the film's suitability for Indian audiences.

cards.headline: Karen Bass Advances to November Runoff for Los Angeles Mayor
cards.teaser: The incumbent will likely face reality star Spencer Pratt in the general election.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advanced from the primary election to the November runoff, finishing in first place but failing to secure the 50% vote share needed to win outright. She will face one of two candidates in the general election.

Spencer Pratt, a former reality television star and Republican newcomer, and Democrat City Council Member Nithya Raman were competing for the second runoff spot. As of election night, Pratt held a significant lead over Raman in early returns, though the second position had not been officially determined.

cards.headline: UK Publishers Can Opt Out of Google AI Search Results
cards.teaser: The Competition and Markets Authority said the change strengthens publishers' negotiating position with Google.
cards.body:
Publishers in the United Kingdom can now opt out of having their content included in Google's AI-powered search features. The Competition and Markets Authority implemented this requirement as a new conduct rule, giving website owners control over whether their material appears in AI features like AI Overviews.

The regulatory decision strengthens publishers' negotiating position with Google regarding content licensing and deals. The change addresses concerns about how AI systems use published content to generate search results and summaries without traditional licensing arrangements.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Praises Paul McCartney's Latest Album
cards.teaser: The pop star said she is never not inspired by the former Beatle's work.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift publicly expressed admiration for Paul McCartney's new album, "The Boys of Dungeon Lane," his first release in five years. Swift said she is never not inspired by McCartney's music, offering praise for the former Beatle's latest work.

McCartney released the album in May, marking his return to recording after a five-year gap. Swift's endorsement highlights the cross-generational appeal of McCartney's music and the continued influence he holds over contemporary artists across different genres.

hero.headline: Secretary of State Rubio questioned on Iran war and gas prices in budget hearings
hero.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio faced questioning from House Democrats during congressional budget hearings about the Trump administration's stance on Israel's nuclear weapons program. Thirty Democratic lawmakers sent a letter to Rubio arguing that the United States must publicly acknowledge that Israel possesses nuclear weapons, particularly as Washington collaborates with Israel on military operations against Iran.

The Democrats, led by Texas Representative Joaquin Castro, contend that the continued ambiguity surrounding Israel's nuclear capabilities is unsustainable given current circumstances. "We are, in the fullest sense, fighting this war side by side with a country whose potential nuclear weapons program the United States government officially refuses to acknowledge," the letter states.

The lawmakers emphasized that Congress needs complete information about the nuclear balance in the Middle East and potential risks of escalation. They noted that the Trump administration has not provided adequate details about planning and contingencies related to nuclear scenarios in the region.

Israel has never publicly confirmed its nuclear weapons program, and no U.S. administration has officially acknowledged it, despite substantial evidence of its existence. The program dates back to the 1950s and received assistance from countries including France and apartheid-era South Africa. American presidents have historically avoided discussing the subject directly.

However, several government officials have essentially confirmed Israel's nuclear capabilities. In a 2006 confirmation hearing, then-nominee Robert Gates said Iran was "surrounded by powers with nuclear weapons: Pakistan to their east, the Russians to the north, the Israelis to the west and us in the Persian Gulf." Similarly, former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert told a German broadcaster that Iran was "aspiring to have nuclear weapons, as America, France, Israel, Russia."

The Democrats pointed out that Israeli officials have occasionally alluded to the weapons. In 2023, Israeli Heritage Minister Amichai Eliyahu suggested using a nuclear bomb in Gaza was "one of the possibilities" following attacks on October 7.

The Democrats noted that Trump administration officials have refused to discuss the issue publicly. When Representative Castro asked Under Secretary of State Thomas DiNanno about Israel's nuclear capabilities at a March congressional hearing, DiNanno declined to answer.

The lawmakers called for consistent treatment of all nations regarding nuclear weapons transparency. "The United States openly acknowledges the nuclear weapons programs of the United Kingdom, France, India, Pakistan, Russia, China, and North Korea. We ask that Israel be held to the same standard as any other foreign country," the letter reads.

The Democrats also warned that continued ambiguity complicates nuclear nonproliferation efforts in the Middle East. Saudi Arabia's crown prince has stated his country would pursue nuclear weapons if Iran develops them, making transparent discussion of Israel's capabilities increasingly important for regional security discussions.

cards.headline: Bill Pulte moves from mortgage chief to acting national intelligence director
cards.teaser: The Senate Intelligence Committee's top Democrat discussed Pulte's transition to the intelligence role.
cards.body:
Bill Pulte, who led the Federal Housing Finance Agency, has been named acting Director of National Intelligence by President Trump. In this role, he will oversee the intelligence community, including the CIA, NSA, and FBI.

Senator Mark Warner of Virginia, the ranking Democrat on the Senate Intelligence Committee, discussed Pulte's appointment in an interview. Pulte's previous work focused on housing and mortgage policy before his move to the intelligence position.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden Cabinet member secured the nomination and could become the first female Native American governor.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. The former Biden administration official is now positioned to compete in the general election this fall.

If elected in November, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in U.S. history.

cards.headline: California governor primary narrows to Becerra and Hilton
cards.teaser: Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton lead the race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton led California's gubernatorial primary, with Democrat Tom Steyer also emerging among the top contenders in early results. The race remained too close to call with many ballots still to be counted.

California's unique primary system allows all candidates to run together regardless of party affiliation, with the top two vote-getters advancing to November's general election. Two Democratic candidates—San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan and former Los Angeles Mayor Antonio Villaraigosa—conceded shortly after polls closed. Governor Gavin Newsom is not seeking reelection.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advances to November runoff
cards.teaser: The first-term Democrat will face a yet-to-be-determined opponent in the general election.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advanced to the general election runoff after finishing ahead in Tuesday's primary, though she fell short of the 50% threshold needed to win outright. She will defend her seat in November as she seeks a second term leading California's largest city.

Bass will face either Republican reality TV star Spencer Pratt or Democrat city council member Nithya Raman in the general election. As of Tuesday evening, the second-place finisher had not yet been determined.

cards.headline: Iowa sets November matchups for Senate and governor races
cards.teaser: Democratic state Representative Josh Turek will face Republican Representative Ashley Hinson for Senate.
cards.body:
Iowa voters selected their nominees for competitive general elections. Democratic state Representative Josh Turek will challenge Republican U.S. Representative Ashley Hinson in the Senate race.

For governor, Democratic state Auditor Rob Sand and Republican businessman Zach Lahn won their respective primaries and will face each other in November. Lahn defeated five challengers including Representative Randy Feenstra. Democrats believe they can be competitive in Iowa's Senate election and the race to replace retiring Republican Governor Kim Reynolds.

cards.headline: Republican support for same-sex marriage drops below 40 percent
cards.teaser: New polling shows a continued decline in GOP backing for marriage equality.
cards.body:
Fewer than four in ten Republicans now say same-sex marriages should be valid under the law, according to a new Gallup Values and Beliefs survey. The polling shows continued decline in Republican support for marriage equality.

The Supreme Court turned away a challenge to its 2015 decision recognizing same-sex marriage nationwide last year, signaling the ruling remains settled law. However, the lead plaintiff in that case and other advocates say the fight for LGBTQ rights continues despite the legal precedent.
